title: The Frogs and the Ox
summary: An old frog sat upon a mossy stone at the edge of a reed-fringed pond, basking in the warm afternoon sun. Suddenly, a colossal ox belonging to a nearby farmer strode down to the wa...
full_text:
An old frog sat upon a mossy stone at the edge of a reed-fringed pond, basking in the warm afternoon sun. Suddenly, a colossal ox belonging to a nearby farmer strode down to the water to drink. With heavy, thunderous steps, the beast trod into the mud, accidentally crushing several tiny froglets beneath his colossal cloven hoof.

One surviving froglet scurried frantically to his mother's stone, gasping for breath: "Oh, Mother! A monster has invaded our pond! It was a beast of impossible size—tall as a hill, with four thick pillars for legs, a tail like a rope, and two sharp crescent horns upon his head!"

The mother frog, puffed up with maternal pride and unwilling to believe that any creature on earth could surpass her own dignity, puffed out her speckled throat: "Was the beast as grand as this?" she croaked, inhaling air until her skin stretched tight.

"Much, much bigger than that, Mother!" cried the little froglet.

The mother inhaled again, swelling her green sides until she was round as a turnip. "Surely he was not as immense as this?"

"Mother, if you burst yourself, you could never equal the tenth part of his majesty!" insisted the child.

Offended by her child's insolence, the foolish old frog took one gigantic, desperate breath, inhaling until her skin was stretched paper-thin. With a loud, pathetic POP, her sides burst asunder, and she perished on the spot, demonstrating the fatal folly of trying to puff oneself up beyond nature's bounds.
moral: Attempting to swell beyond your natural measure brings ruin and disgrace.
